en.name: Philip Neri
en.summary: Roman priest known as the "Apostle of Rome" and the "Humorous Saint" for combining deep holiness with playful joy.
en.body: Philip Neri left a comfortable family business in his youth to live simply in Rome, spending years as a layman informally ministering to pilgrims, the sick, and the poor before being persuaded, somewhat reluctantly, to be ordained a priest. He became famous throughout Rome for a distinctive spiritual style built on humor, practical jokes, and evident joy rather than austerity, believing that cheerfulness was itself a spiritual strength, and he often used playful humility, wearing outlandish clothing or shaving half his beard, to deflate excessive admiration directed at him. He founded the Congregation of the Oratory, a community of priests living together without formal vows, dedicated to prayer, preaching, and care of the young people and pilgrims flooding into Counter-Reformation Rome. He died in 1595 and was canonized in 1622, remembered as one of the most beloved and approachable saints of his era.
